text:
morgan: quick q — i'm about to land a terraform change that routes customer egress TLS through our new sidecar proxy (NLB -> proxy -> svc). want to double-check healthcheck target/port and secret wiring before i apply.

zane: can you paste the service/ingress snippet? also are we preserving client ip on the NLB?

morgan: pasted below — plan is to keep ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local on the svc and use nodeport for proxy. trying to avoid double-termination.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-egress
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  selector:
    app: inference-proxy
  ports:
    - name: tls
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      protocol: TCP
```

jia: looks reasonable. two checks: 1) make sure the readiness probe for the proxy binds to targetPort (8443) or else kube will mark pods NotReady and NLB won't have nodes. 2) secret for certs needs to be mounted on the proxy pod, not the backend svc — confirm terraform maps the secret name unchanged.

morgan: yes readiness currently hits :8443/ready. terraform will create aws_lb_target_group with port=443 and target_type=ip -> targets point to nodeport 8443? that's the tricky part. i'm considering using target_type=instance and nodeport mapping.

sam: if you use target_type=ip we have to register pod IPs and ensure kube-proxy preserves iptables so healthchecks work. instance is simpler for Local externalTrafficPolicy but has rollover complexity when nodes scale.

zane: also note ALB/NLB healthcheck behavior — NLB healthchecks hit the node (or pod) on the configured target port. if you configure TG port=443 but node has 8443 listening, you need TG to use port 8443 or use proxy protocol.

morgan: good catch. current terraform had TG.port = 443; i'll change it to 8443 -> can someone confirm that doesn't break TLS passthrough semantics?

jia: fine as long as TLS stays passthrough on the LB and proxy does termination. TG port can be 8443. just ensure security groups allow 8443 from LB subnets.

infra-bot: deploy-check: terraform plan for infra/egress-proxy returned: 2 changes (1 modify target_group, 1 modify target_group_attachment). diff: TG.port 443 -> 8443. link: https://ci.example.com/plan/9843 :eyes:

morgan: thanks infra-bot. i'll update the TF var docs. also need to wire secret -> proxy pod: current k8s manifest mounts secret name inference-egress-cert. terraform aws-secretsmanager resource is named inference/egress-cert in state; confirm mapping.

zane: make sure k8s secret is created in the same namespace by the k8s provider or via the helm chart. i've seen mismatches where the secret exists but name contains a suffix from helmrelease.

morgan: plan: 1) change TG.port to 8443 in terraform 2) add SG rule for 8443 from LB subnets 3) verify k8s secret name exact match in helm values 4) run a short canary (2 pods) in staging with ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local then roll.

sam: for the canary, add an ingress annotation to skip connection draining during test (so we don't get 502 noise). also add a quick grafana dashboard row for 5xxs for that svc.

ops-bot: alert-note: recent rollout to prod with similar TG.port change caused a transient 502 when readiness endpoint returned 503 for 45s. set a 30s grace period on the probe to avoid flapping.

morgan: ack — i'll bump readiness initialDelaySeconds to 20 and timeout/period to 5. keeping probe logic tolerant while canary warms.

zane: one more: update the terraform state import docs — if you switch target_type from instance -> ip you'll need to recreate TG attachments. prefer modifying port only.

morgan: ok will do only port change for minimal disruption. pushing PR now: https://git.example.com/redwood/infra/pulls/4521 :thumbsup:

jia: LGTM, thanks. ping here when plan is applied and we watch staging for 15m.

morgan: will monitor, will post results. :shipit:
